answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a decision, then slash that bond when independent audits expose duplicate-controlled identities or provable abuse. The bond does not prove a personhood, but it makes mass identity creation costly: an attacker must lock real capital in every account and risk losing it. Even if agents wander from one task to another, the same stake remains exposed from dawn to the final audit at the wharf.
